Observed: exit 0; 2 independent occurrence-safety tests and all 14 archive law tests passed, no ignored tests. The independent tests inject providers that fail on any call, then verify duplicate-key, absent-key, invalid-scale, and stored-failure lookups never consult either provider under Packed or Recomputable. They also swap two distinct input rows sharing exactly the same key, verify the key sequence remains identical but the input reference changes, and observe SourceMismatch. The law suite's printed failing seeds belong to intentionally falsified mutants, including first-occurrence aliasing; the enclosing tests passed. Receipt: /private/tmp/eyes4s-ui-e-independent-review/repair-adversarial-laws.log and .log.meta.json. Combined fresh evidence: 50 passing tests/laws.

Source inspection confirms roundtrip generators now include repeated keys (laws/DensityArchiveLawSuite.scala:127-134) and the suite explicitly falsifies a provider that aliases every repeated key to its first occurrence (:272-293). Key-only map-identity laws retain their unique-key domain, consistent with intentional ambiguity refusal.

Reused unchanged HDR evidence from the parent: 9 passing tests, including 1,320 independent exact integer threshold-set comparisons across 165 four-cell distributions and refusal of full coverage for total0.875. Verified MassLevels implementation and existing suite unchanged across this repair. No new HDR run or broader numerical claim.

Limits: bounded source review and focused JVM evidence only. Full author gates/audit were reported running, not passed, at assignment; this review does not establish those gates, JS qualification, shared publishing-consumer success, manifest integration, UI behavior, or landing acceptance. No main/author-source edits, merge, push, Mote acceptance transition, or UI-D change. Detached review copy verified at the exact head/tree; tracked sources unchanged, with only independent test files and local sbt-git workaround untracked. Verdict does not transfer to a later SHA.
